scope: Proposition 7.9 (Macroscopic form of the resampling density) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite stable decomposition and restrict its macroscopic parameters to a compact set on which all noise durations are positive, all randomized first displacements are strictly inside their support, and the reference height density is positive. Include among the macroscopic nuisance variables the frozen contour pieces, integrated ordinary pieces, and the conditional noise contours. Fix a subsequential limiting law of the actual frozen data. The continuity cells can be chosen so that, for almost every frozen value under this law and every sequence of frozen data converging to that value, the density in Equation (7.7), after multiplication by its common power of N and fixed lattice factor, converges in the form required by Lemma 7.4. Its limit depends only on the macroscopic variables. On every cell containing a compatible strict path tube, its limiting normalizing integral is positive. Here finite frozen data range over atoms having positive probability in the chosen stable cell. In particular, a suffix-type atom comes with an actual compatible word in that cell for the protected-rank comparison.
